**My thinking, as Wang Jianguo, farmer, Quzhou County:**

I've been working this land since I was a young man. My father grew wheat and maize, I grow wheat and maize, and that's how it works here on the North China Plain. The soil is good loam, we have a motor pump on the well, and the county supply cooperative sells decent seed. My wife helps with spraying and my son is in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly just me.

I have 10 mu of contracted land. I'll do the full wheat-maize double crop rotation — winter wheat planted in October after I till, then summer maize direct-seeded right after wheat harvest in June, same ground. No point trying cotton or vegetables at my scale without the market connections.

For wheat I'll buy Jimai 22 seed from the cooperative — it's an improved variety the extension station has been pushing for years, good lodging resistance. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and then chase it with urea at jointing. Three irrigations: one right after sowing to get germination, one at jointing, one at heading. If I skip one I risk losing 50 kg/mu yield easily.

For maize I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid again — it's what everyone around here uses and I know how it behaves. I direct seed into the wheat stubble to save time, no deep tillage between crops. Only irrigate if July is dry at silking. One herbicide pass when maize is knee-high, then one fungicide/insecticide spray around tasseling.

I won't push yields above what this land can do. 450 on wheat, 550 on maize — that's what I've averaged the last few years.
